This interim guidance on Ebola event management at points of entry (PoE) was prepared by WHO in collaboration with experts from WHO, the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), the International Air Transport Association (IATA), and the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). The guidance is intended for National Focal Points for the International Health Regulations (IHR) (2005), public health authorities at PoE, PoE operators, conveyance operators, crew members, and other stakeholders involved in managing public health events. It should be used as a reference alongside WHO publications on contingency planning at PoE, local established capacities, and emergency plans. The content should be adapted to the current situation, local requirements, and common practices. To reduce the risk of infectious travelers boarding aircraft or other modes of transportation and to minimize disruptions to PoE operations, the following measures should be implemented: 1. For countries with Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) transmission: Conduct exit screening of all individuals at international airports, seaports, and major land crossings for unexplained febrile illness consistent with potential Ebola infection. At a minimum, this screening should include a questionnaire, temperature measurement, and, if fever is present, an assessment of the risk that the fever is caused by EVD. 2. For all points of entry: Ensure a public health emergency contingency plan is in place at each designated PoE. For international airports, the aerodrome emergency plan should include a public health component in accordance with ICAO health-related requirements. Allocate a designated area at PoE for health assessments in the event of suspected illness detected in a traveler. Establish standard operating procedures for referring ill travelers to designated hospitals, including identifying adequate ambulance services. 3. Public health emergency plans and standard operating procedures: These should align with international best practices, agreements, and the IHR. The aim is to enable early detection of potentially infected individuals, assist in implementing WHO recommendations related to Ebola management, and prevent the international spread of the disease while avoiding unnecessary restrictions and delays at PoE. 4. Staffing and equipment: Ensure a sufficient number of trained staff with appropriate and adequate personal protective equipment (PPE) and disinfectants. Raise awareness among conveyance operators about the need to notify PoE health authorities immediately upon identifying any suspected cases before arrival. Ensure passenger locator forms are available on flights and at airports, and that airport ground staff and flight crews are trained in managing EVD and environmental contaminants. 5. Communication and awareness: Maintain effective and rapid communication between PoE health authorities and the national health surveillance system. Disseminate information about EVD to all relevant stakeholders at PoE. 6. Management of events during travel: If a potential case is detected during travel, the response should depend on the nature of the exposure, the status of global alerts, and the awareness of various parties involved. For symptomatic travelers or crew members, assess the time and date of illness onset, travel history, and any contact with suspected or confirmed EVD cases. If the traveler has recently been to an EVD-affected area and exhibits symptoms, the PoE health authority should activate the public health emergency plan, arrange medical examinations, and transport suspected cases to designated hospitals. 7. Onboard management: If symptoms consistent with EVD are identified onboard an aircraft or ship, assess the environment for contamination (e.g., vomit, blood, or other body fluids) and determine the number of exposed passengers and staff. Ensure the captain or master is informed, and notify PoE authorities. For aircraft, ensure access to ground-based medical support and provide medical assistance during the flight if necessary. Upon arrival, ensure appropriate precautions are taken for the disembarkation of ill and healthy travelers. 8. Post-arrival actions: If a traveler has recently been to an EVD-affected area and exhibits symptoms, collect information from the crew regarding any medical assistance provided during travel. Arrange for a medical assessment upon arrival and ensure space is available for interviews and health assessments, with access to toilet facilities and seating. Collect clinical specimens and/or environmental samples as needed, following national practices. 9. Coordination and preparedness: Public health authorities should coordinate with PoE operators, conveyance operators, and other stakeholders to ensure sufficient availability of staff, PPE, and disinfectants. They should also provide regional or national public health contact information and identify interpreters if needed. 10. Documentation and reporting: For air travel, ensure the availability of passenger locator forms and the health part of the aircraft general declaration. For maritime travel, ensure the availability of maritime health declarations, ship sanitation certificates, and medical logbooks. By implementing these measures, PoE health authorities can effectively manage EVD-related events, minimize the risk of disease transmission, and maintain the safety of travelers and staff.
